meta.title: Operation of Mechanical Sieve Shaker in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To separate crude drug powders into defined particle size fractions using mechanically oscillated standard test sieves for pharmacopeial powder grade determination and particle size analysis.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for pharmacopeial sieve analysis of crude drug powders and verification of powder grade (coarse, fine, very fine) per IP/WHO standards.
procedure: Select the standard sieve set corresponding to the required IP powder grades (typically No. 10, No. 22, No. 44, No. 85, No. 120 sieves).
Clean all sieves with a soft natural-bristle brush to remove any residue from previous use.
Inspect sieves for damaged mesh, holes, or bent frames — replace damaged sieves before use.
Stack sieves in descending aperture order (largest at top, smallest at bottom) with a collecting pan at the base.
Mount the sieve stack securely in the mechanical sieve shaker clamps.
Accurately weigh the drug powder sample (typically 50 g) and record the weight.
Place the sample on the topmost sieve and place the lid on top.
Set the shaker amplitude and operating time: typically 10–15 minutes at standard amplitude for pharmacopeial analysis.
Switch on the mechanical shaker and allow the full programmed run to complete.
After completion, switch off and wait for all movement to cease before handling the sieves.
Carefully dismantle the sieve stack; transfer the retained material from each sieve to a pre-weighed container.
Weigh the material retained on each sieve and in the collecting pan.
Verify: sum of all fractions should equal the initial sample weight ± 1% (loss acceptable limit).
Calculate the percentage retained on each sieve; record against IP specifications for the tested drug.
Clean all sieves immediately with a soft brush after use; wash if needed and dry completely.
Record sieve numbers, retained weights, percentages, and powder grade conclusion in the logbook.
precautions: Never clean sieves with metal brushes or wire — this distorts the mesh apertures.
Wear a dust mask when loading and unloading powders.
Do not overload sieves — excessive sample weight prevents proper separation.
Ensure the sieve stack is securely clamped — loose sieves during mechanical shaking can fall.
Do not use damaged or corroded sieves for official pharmacopeial testing — results will be invalid.
Store sieves in individual protective containers to preserve mesh integrity.
Calibrate sieve apertures annually using reference wire gauges or optical measurement.
Allow the shaker to come to a complete stop before removing the sieve assembly.
